title: Welcome and Table of Contents
summary: What SS1 Economics First Term is about, how to use the notes, and a map of every unit.

p: Economics is the study of how people, businesses and governments make choices when resources are limited. Every day you make economic choices: how to spend your pocket money, whether to buy food or a book, how to use your time. Economics helps you to understand these choices and the way your community and country earn and spend money.

In First Term you will learn what economics is, the tools economists use (tables, averages, graphs and charts), how demand and supply work, how goods are produced, how work is shared among workers, how different countries organise their economies, the types of business, the size of the population and the labour market.

Each unit has simple notes, tables, diagrams and worked examples. Read slowly, and copy the tables and graphs into your notebook. At the end of every unit there are practice questions. They do not count towards a mark; they help you to check that you understood. Answer them all correctly to complete the unit.
Economics is also an examination subject in WAEC and NECO, so learn the key words in each unit: you will meet them again in the exam.

sections.h: Table of contents for First Term
p: The units follow the scheme of work. Week 5 is the midterm examination and Week 7 is the midterm break.
Note: in the weekly scheme, topics are placed on given weeks. Some units cover more than one week of the scheme.

p: Read the newspaper or listen to the news and ask yourself which economic idea you can see in it. Practise drawing graphs neatly with a ruler and pencil. Learn each definition word for word and then say it in your own words. When you answer essay questions, define the term, explain it with a Nigerian example and then give a conclusion.

activity: In your notebook, write down three choices you made this week that involved money or time. For each one, say what you gave up (this is called the opportunity cost).
